html:
In 1863 King Norodom signed a treaty at Oudong putting Cambodia under the protection of France. He hoped France would shield his small kingdom from Siam and Vietnam, which had long fought over it.

France took more and more control, and from 1887 Cambodia was part of French Indochina. Siam returned the western provinces, including Angkor, in 1907, and French scholars began to restore the temples.

Taxes and forced labour fell heavily on peasants, and few Cambodians got schooling. Independence came in 1953 under King Norodom Sihanouk, as France lost the First Indochina War.
